q7.answer: Confirm runs in one transaction: move the pending secret into user_totp (overwriting the old one on replace), set last_step to the confirming code's step, delete all old recovery codes and insert 10 new hashed ones, delete every other session of the user (keeping the current one), and delete the pending row. If it fails partway, it rolls back completely: the user stays as before and no recovery codes are shown.

q8.answer: It is a login_challenges row (token_hash, user_id, created_at, expires_at = +5 min, failures). The browser refers to it with a separate httponly, secure, SameSite=Lax mfa cookie (max_age 300) holding a new_token(32), stored hashed, and never accepted as a session. It is removed on success, on the 5th wrong entry, or on expiry, with the cookie cleared and the user sent back to the password form.

q9.answer: The secret is in user_totp.secret_sealed (sealed with seal()). Enrolment status is the existing confirmed row in user_totp, while an unconfirmed secret sits in totp_pending, which sign-in never reads. The replay guard is user_totp.last_step, and recovery codes are hashed rows in recovery_codes with used_at. 2FA is on exactly when the user has a confirmed user_totp row.

q10.answer: The old authenticator stays active in user_totp, and the replacement secret sits inert in totp_pending, which sign-in ignores, so sign-in is unchanged during the replacement. If the user abandons it, the old authenticator keeps working and the pending row is simply left, then overwritten by the next setup or deleted on cancel or on disable. The diagram has a cancel transition from ReplacePending back to On. I did not decide any expiry or cleanup job for stale pending rows.

q11.answer: The server tries the input first as an authenticator code, then as a recovery code, and accepts a recovery code only if it matches an unused one. Yes, any wrong entry, including a wrong recovery code, increments the challenge's failures counter toward the 5 limit. I did not specify a input-format check, such as telling them apart by length.
